rederivationScript.runtime: about 18 s, single process, python3 + numpy (numpy only to read checkpoint buffers); read-only

verdictSummary: No discrepancy. Every number in report.json (64 pair scores, 32 unit values and flags, 4 founder rows, readings, 8 pooled blocks, the whole-block bootstrap, the descriptive roster items) was re-derived from the 1,536 raw result files and the roster, with exact rational arithmetic, and agrees to a maximum absolute difference of 2.22e-16 (float rounding). The study is technically complete by the protocol's definition. All four founders read 'not met'; cluster-33 therefore reads 'not met' in the M4 table (inconclusive, not evidence of a stall, cannot support the physics-change pivot) and the cluster-16 clause is not triggered. The qualifications below concern what 'not met' can and cannot carry, not the arithmetic.
method: Independent Python re-derivation (review-rederive.py); it does not call or port the TypeScript analyzer. It (1) verifies the pin chain (report, protocol, roster, candidate, release, manifest, forecast, 65 execution sources, 64 receipts) and recomputes the study identity and the roster payload hash; (2) indexes all 1,536 raw assay files by content, recomputes each cache key from the roster hexes and the frozen study's own cfg, recomputes every score from the recorded masses and every provenance record; (3) regenerates all 128 type-matched null genomes bit for bit from (H, L) with my own Mulberry32 (seeds 6490100 + j); (4) re-derives all 64 H genomes (500k ancestors) in a third implementation directly from the 64 checkpoints and the mutation-edge deltas of the 32 normal histories, after verifying the receipt chain and every edge/checkpoint file hash; (5) recomputes every estimand with exact Fractions then floats (genome mean of 8 competitions, two nulls per pair, two pairs per unit, L - N with lower bound L lower - N upper, certification lower > 0.10 strictly, late-certification, founder-level L / N / contrast, readings in the protocol's fixed order), the pooled block rule and the whole-block bootstrap (seed 6490300, 10,000 resamples, my own Mulberry32 and JS summation order); (6) recomputes the descriptive roster items and the protocol's pre-run facts from the roster; (7) checks technical completeness from the raw evidence (replays, audits, ledger, supervisor log, lock/stop/tmp state); (8) cross-checks the already-written continuation-findings.md tables. Reads only; the single optional --out writes JSON to a path the caller names (I used my scratch directory).

qualifications.detail: 'Not met' is a failure to clear a 7-of-8 rule, not a finding of no effect or of a stall. The protocol's power paragraph assumed a unit-contrast SD of 0.15-0.4; the observed sample SDs are 0.395 (cluster-33), 0.488 (cluster-4, above the assumed range), 0.220 (cluster-139), 0.107 (cluster-16). Post hoc illustration, not a decision rule: if cluster-33's units were independent Normal at the observed mean (0.427) and SD (0.395), the chance of 7-of-8 would be about 0.49; at the observed certified fraction (5/8) it would be 0.135. So the result is consistent with real but uneven post-sweep gains and with no general gain, which is what the findings text and the protocol's table say.

Heterogeneity across seeds dominates cluster-33: unit L - N values are 0.065, 0.562, 0.195, 0.878, 0.693, 0.012, 0.041, 0.971 (three near zero, four above 0.5). L vs H is 0.18, 0.59, 0.02, 0.82, 0.70, -0.14, 0.01, 0.91. Post hoc: the three uncertified units (6410001, 006, 007) all have an H that already carries the swept bias (94, 99 -> 119, 82), whereas the one seed with no sweep at all (6410002) is among the clearer gains (L 0.587, L - N 0.562); among the seven seeds whose first sweep was complete by 500k (the protocol's clean case) 4 are certified (003, 004, 005, 008) and 4 are late-certified (001, 004, 005, 008). The pooled founder-level contrast (0.43) is carried by a few seeds, which is exactly why the protocol fixed a per-seed rule.

'Certified' (L - N > 0.10) is not progress. The null N is on average a damaged H (founder-level N vs H: -0.041, -0.101, -0.028, -0.101 for cluster-33, 4, 16, 139), so L - N can clear 0.10 while L itself does not beat H: four units are certified but not late-certified (33/6410003 L 0.024; 16/6410003 L 0.070; 139/6410001 L 0.045; 139/6410002 L -0.073 against N -0.558). The protocol's separate late-certified count exists for this reason; here both counts fall below 7 for every founder, so the reading does not depend on the difference. The no-adaptation reference cluster-16 was certified in 1 of 8 units (6410003), a chance-level event.

The 9/256 per-test tail is optimistic (shared founder, the same four assay seeds, and 10 of 32 units whose two pairs share one H; 7 of the 13 certified units are shared-H units, post hoc count). Optimism inflates false positives; no test was met, so it does not touch any reading. 'Certified' means the observed mean exceeds 0.10 with nothing missing: all bounds collapse to the point value, so no sampling uncertainty is carried. A unit's N is the mean of 4 null genomes whose means have SD 0.30 (cluster-33), 0.36 (cluster-4), 0.30 (cluster-139), 0.09 (cluster-16), so a unit's N has a standard error of about 0.15-0.18 (post hoc) against a threshold of 0.10; the closest unit contrast to the threshold is 139/6410001 at 0.126.

cluster-139's founder-level L vs H (0.103) comes from two seeds (6410007: 0.520, 6410008: 0.220); the other six are between -0.07 and 0.05. In 6410007 both pairs gained the mu sweep after 500k (33 -> 47), so part of that advantage is the sweep itself, as the protocol anticipated. In 6410008 one pair has no mu sweep (33 -> 33) and one has (54 -> 54).

cluster-4: L loses to its own 500k ancestor in 5 of 8 seeds (-0.381, -0.518, -0.319, -0.110, -0.121 in seeds 1, 2, 4, 5, 8) while its founder-lineage mass rose 1.01M -> 1.07M. Head-to-head and abundance proxies therefore disagree for this founder in most seeds (descriptive; non-transitivity of the gradient competition is possible and not tested).

The replays and audits (8 configurations, 39 audit re-runs) re-execute only the frozen originals, whose ancestor is a founder. None of the 1,536 new configurations (ancestor = a 500k genome) was ever re-run, so run-to-run determinism for them rests on the same pinned executor, not on a replay of their own; I could not re-execute anything (GPU forbidden). The collector's own validation (not re-derived here) recomputes each result's initial-state hash from its genomes; I verified only that all 1,536 initial and final state hashes are distinct and every score follows from the recorded masses. The protocol discloses that no non-founder-ancestor competition had run before; no invocation failed.

The fixed reading text for 'not met' ('no evidence that change since the midpoint beats random change of the same size') labels failure of the 7-of-8 rule. It should not be quoted as 'no evidence' for cluster-33: the observed founder-level contrast is 0.43 and 5 of 8 units clear 0.10 (descriptive). The protocol itself adds that it is not evidence that adaptation stopped.

The H -> L change is small (median 7-17 of 163 slots), so the nulls are small perturbations of an adapted genome; about half of the individual null genomes beat H (null genome means > 0: 17 of 32, 10 of 32, 14 of 32, 15 of 32 for clusters 33, 4, 16, 139), so 'random change is neutral to mildly harmful' holds for the mean, not for individual nulls. Leave-one-assay-seed-out changes no certified or late-certified count for any founder (post hoc); the assignment-0 and assignment-1 arm means differ by at most 0.055 (largest for the cluster-33 and cluster-4 nulls), and averaging both positions is built into every genome mean.

Results are conditional (as the protocol says) on the four deliberately discovered founders, single-founder chambers, the gradient competition, the fixed assay seeds, and a 500k midpoint chosen once. The pooled block rule (7 of 8 blocks, mean 0.170, bootstrap [0.119, 0.218]) is descriptive, includes the no-adaptation reference founder, and block 6410008 (0.232) is carried by cluster-33's 0.971; it plays no part in any reading.

notChecked: No simulation or competition was re-run (GPU forbidden). Raw masses are taken as recorded; see Q7.

I did not re-run the Deno tests, re-read the 54 frozen + 11 runner source files for correctness (only that their SHA-256s equal the candidate's pins on the current tree), or recompute state hashes / conservation / biology checks of the checkpoint chain (the frozen loader's job; I verified the receipt chain, the edge-delta and checkpoint file hashes and the lineage/mass tables).

My genome sampler and Mulberry32 follow the library's semantics read from tools/lib/discovery-divergence-control.ts and founder-policy.ts; the bit-for-bit match shows the roster implements that sampler, not that it is the only reasonable reading of the protocol's wording.
Absence of any interim analysis is inferred only from report.json being the sole analysis output and being newer than every run artifact.
Whether the gradient competition is biologically meaningful, whether four founders generalize, and the plan-level substitution for the 'amended endpoint 2' were not judged.
